info.name: Pages
info.summary: Edit, review and publish a Jekyll site from Nextcloud
info.description:
# Pages
Pages turns Nextcloud into the editing surface for a Jekyll site and takes it all the way to publication.
## What the app does
- Authors write their own pages **with Nextcloud's own file API**, so version history, trash, sharing, desktop sync and activity all keep working - Rebuilds the site preview as authors save and shows it in the same page - Reviewers approve a page for the site and publish it: the publish is the git commit, and a push follows when a git remote is configured - Reads the deployment as facts: head, commits the remote is ahead, unpublished files
## Deployment model
**This app is the control plane; a companion service is the data plane.**
Nextcloud PHP cannot execute host binaries, and it must not be given the power to start host processes. So the work that needs a real shell — mirroring the source into a working copy, running the site generator, and driving git — is done by `pages-bridge`, a small zero-dependency Python service that runs on the same host.
The administrator installs that service once and pairs it from the Pages settings with a one-time code: the app generates both secrets, discovers the data directory and pushes the whole configuration. From then on this app owns the configuration of the instance's one site.
Nothing is installed or started behind your back: enabling this app never touches files outside its own data directory.
## Current scope
Targets self-hosted deployments where the administrator can run a small service on the Nextcloud host. Instances that forbid `exec` and cannot run such a service fall back to a read/write editor without build or publish.
